name: Tabitha “Sixshot” Wren
origin: Lands beyond Cador and the Eccentric East
appearance: A wiry, energetic gnome with unruly copper-brown hair, sharp green eyes, and a seemingly permanent smudge of grease somewhere on her face. Tabitha wears a well-worn leather apron over a rolled-sleeve shirt, with numerous pockets containing springs, tools, bolts, and peculiar mechanical contraptions. A heavily modified six-shooter hangs from her hip.
portrayal: Tabitha is excitable, inventive, and endlessly curious. She speaks rapidly, particularly when discussing her craft, and frequently interrupts herself upon having a new idea. She has little patience for conventional thinking and takes considerable delight in demonstrating her latest inventions, regardless of whether they work as intended. She is fond of terrible puns and has a competitive streak when it comes to marksmanship.
motivations: Tabitha regards her workshop at the Wayward Spur as an opportunity to pursue her craft without the inconveniences of making a living on the road. She is driven by the satisfaction of solving mechanical problems and creating things that nobody has made before. She takes particular interest in the experiences of adventurers who field-test her creations, though she is sometimes more concerned with the performance of her ammunition than the circumstances in which it was used.
personal_circumstances: A former adventurer and accomplished marksman, Tabitha developed a fascination with mechanical crossbows, ingenious firing mechanisms, and unusual ammunition during her travels. Her nickname originated from her ability to put six bolts into a target before most marksmen could loose two. Having encountered numerous traditions of weaponsmithing throughout her adventuring career, she is familiar with the Qasari origins of the six-shooter's repeating mechanism and finds the Cadorian belief that it is their own invention rather amusing.
relationships: Tabitha shares a friendly professional rivalry with Sazerac Martini, frequently contrasting his reverence for traditional craftsmanship with her enthusiasm for innovation. She enjoys exchanging exaggerated tales of adventuring exploits with Flopthar and remains fascinated, if somewhat bewildered, by Madame Zoria's divinations. She is genuinely fond of Floyd and grateful for the freedom afforded to her at the Spur.
knowledge_and_rumors: Tabitha sells, repairs, and modifies bows, crossbows, and six-shooters, and maintains a selection of mundane and alchemical specialty ammunition. She can fashion certain varieties of magical ammunition, though more powerful enchantments require rare components that are not readily available. She frequently offers modest rewards for unusual materials, unfamiliar weapons, and recovered mechanical designs. Adventurers may also commission custom ammunition or modifications to their ranged weapons.
source_profile:
Tabitha "Sixshot" Wren — Bowsmith
Chaotic Good, female gnome, middle-aged

Appearance. A wiry, energetic gnome with unruly copper-brown hair, sharp green eyes, and a
seemingly permanent smudge of grease somewhere on her face. Tabitha wears a well-worn

leather apron over a rolled-sleeve shirt, with numerous pockets containing springs, tools, bolts,
and peculiar mechanical contraptions. A heavily modified six-shooter hangs from her hip.

Portrayal. Tabitha is excitable, inventive, and endlessly curious. She speaks rapidly, particularly
when discussing her craft, and frequently interrupts herself upon having a new idea. She has
little patience for conventional thinking and takes considerable delight in demonstrating her
latest inventions, regardless of whether they work as intended. She is fond of terrible puns and
has a competitive streak when it comes to marksmanship.

Background. A former adventurer and accomplished marksman, Tabitha developed a
fascination with mechanical crossbows, ingenious firing mechanisms, and unusual ammunition
during her travels. Her nickname originated from her ability to put six bolts into a target before
most marksmen could loose two. Having encountered numerous traditions of weaponsmithing
throughout her adventuring career, she is familiar with the Qasari origins of the six-shooter's
repeating mechanism and finds the Cadorian belief that it is their own invention rather amusing.

Motivations. Tabitha regards her workshop at the Wayward Spur as an opportunity to pursue
her craft without the inconveniences of making a living on the road. She is driven by the
satisfaction of solving mechanical problems and creating things that nobody has made before.
She takes particular interest in the experiences of adventurers who field-test her creations,
though she is sometimes more concerned with the performance of her ammunition than the
circumstances in which it was used.

Relationships. Tabitha shares a friendly professional rivalry with Sazerac Martini, frequently
contrasting his reverence for traditional craftsmanship with her enthusiasm for innovation. She
enjoys exchanging exaggerated tales of adventuring exploits with Flopthar and remains
fascinated, if somewhat bewildered, by Madame Zoria's divinations. She is genuinely fond of
Floyd and grateful for the freedom afforded to her at the Spur.

Services and Expertise. Tabitha sells, repairs, and modifies bows, crossbows, and
six-shooters, and maintains a selection of mundane and alchemical specialty ammunition. She
can fashion certain varieties of magical ammunition, though more powerful enchantments
require rare components that are not readily available. She frequently offers modest rewards for
unusual materials, unfamiliar weapons, and recovered mechanical designs. Adventurers may
also commission custom ammunition or modifications to their ranged weapons.

Adventure Hooks.

   ●​ A Better Mousetrap. Tabitha commissions the recovery of a rare mineral or a lost
      mechanical blueprint that she believes could facilitate the development of a novel
      repeating-crossbow design.
   ●​ Field Testing. Tabitha provides an adventuring party with a small quantity of
      experimental ammunition at no charge, on the condition that they test it under particular
      circumstances and report their findings upon returning to the Spur.
source_reference: Handbook v0.4, pp. 17–18; newer staff entry supersedes Legendarium index
